_doc: The Whisper Network (scripts/mission/rumours.gd, docs/GDD.md 'Campaign'). A rumour is carried by named townsfolk of data/npcs.json (its `carriers`); every dawn it spreads along the `network` links (each carrier passes it to each neighbour with probability `spread` x the channel boost x (1 - crackdown/200)). reach = carriers / roster, in percent. At reach >= `threshold` (default 35) its `effects` apply once ('it takes hold'). A false rumour that has taken hold may be disproved each dawn (chance `disprove` x reach/100): `disproved` effects apply, and if the player planted it the channel's faction loses influence. A planted rumour may be traced to the player each dawn (channel `trace` x (1 + crackdown/100) x reach/100): notoriety +12, crackdown +3. At night each carrier present in the square says the rumour (intel.gd overhearing: stand within 4 m for 5 s); heard rumours go to Mission.journal.rumours and the Log ('rumour: ...'). `truth`: true, false, or a campaign condition string (e.g. 'lever:hauer_debts') evaluated when the rumour is planted or tested. `person`: following this lead (day panel) brings that person into the night (data/campaign.json people). `plantable` rumours can be planted from the day panel through a channel (data/campaign.json channels). `seed`: network groups it starts in. `start`: in play from the first day. `kind` (omen, miracle, curse, relic, prophecy: superstition and religion) multiplies the spread through the network groups in `kind_spread` (fastest among the street and the pious, slowest in the salon); planting a superstition costs Salon influence (`superstition_salon_cost`); a staged miracle that is traced is blasphemy (`blasphemy`).

deserter_tannery.subject: A deserter
deserter_tannery.text: A Polish deserter from the Austrian line hides among the tanners of Garbary, beyond the west gate.
line: W Garbarach, u garbarzy, siedzi dezerter od Austriaków. Nie chce wracać.
In Garbary, among the tanners, sits a deserter from the Austrians. He won't go back.

corporal_laundress.subject: The Corporal
corporal_laundress.source: the women at the west well
corporal_laundress.text: Corporal Brandt keeps a laundress, Marianna, by the drying lines in the north-west corner. She hates him and washes his shirts.
line: Kapral chodzi do praczki Marianny, tej od sznurów przy Winiarni. Ona go nie cierpi.
The Corporal visits Marianna the laundress, by the lines at the Winiarnia. She can't stand him.

russian_coffee.subject: A Russian
russian_coffee.text: A Russian with too much money reads the Gazette at the coffee house on the south row every night.
line: W kawiarni siedzi Moskal, co płaci złotem za kawę. Czyta gazetę do góry nogami.
In the coffee house sits a Muscovite who pays gold for coffee. Reads his paper upside down.

crier_price.subject: The town crier
crier_price.text: Wit the town crier will cry anything for four złoty and a bottle. He stands at the Town Hall front after the bell.
line: Wit, obwoływacz, wykrzyczy wszystko za cztery złote i flaszkę.
Wit the crier will shout anything for four złoty and a bottle.

bishop_mistress.subject: The Bishop
bishop_mistress.text: The Bishop keeps a Russian mistress in Kanonicza street. (If this spreads, the Church suffers with him.)
line: Biskup trzyma Moskalkę na Kanoniczej. Wszyscy wiedzą.
The Bishop keeps a Russian woman on Kanonicza. Everybody knows.

effects.text: The tale of the Bishop's Russian mistress is in every tavern; the canons blame the movement.

disproved.text: The Bishop's 'mistress' turned out to be his widowed sister. The slander dies.

dragon_wawel.subject: The dragon
dragon_wawel.text: The Wawel dragon has come back up from his cave and eats only Austrians.
line: Smok wrócił spod Wawelu. Je tylko Austriaków, bo Polacy za chudzi.
The dragon is back from under Wawel. Eats only Austrians: Poles are too thin.

effects.text: Children sing that the dragon eats Austrians. Soldiers pretend not to hear; the street laughs.

salt_tax.subject: The salt excise
salt_tax.text: The Austrian excise will double the salt tax at the New Year.
line: Od Nowego Roku akcyza na sól podwójna. Z czego żyć?
From the New Year the salt excise doubles. What are we to live on?

effects.text: The salt excise is all the market talks of. The guilds grumble louder than they dare.

apprentice_press.subject: The printer's apprentice
apprentice_press.text: The printer's apprentice, Tadeusz, a Jacobin, sets type at night in a cellar on Jagiellońska by the Collegium.
line: Czeladnik drukarza, Tadek, składa czcionki nocą przy Kolegium. Jakobin, mówią.
The printer's journeyman, Tadek, sets type at night by the Collegium. A Jacobin, they say.

banker_little_market.subject: A Prussian banker
banker_little_market.text: A Prussian banker on the Little Market, east of St Mary's, holds half the Austrian officers' notes, the Commissioner's among them.
line: Pruski bankier na Małym Rynku ma weksle połowy oficerów. I komisarza.
A Prussian banker on the Little Market holds half the officers' notes. And the Commissioner's.

fence_fish_market.subject: A fence
fence_fish_market.text: A fence at the fish market by the Vistula quays buys anything with a lock on it, and sells the keys.
line: Na targu rybnym pod Wisłą jest paser. Kupi każdy zamek, sprzeda każdy klucz.
At the fish market by the Vistula there's a fence. Buys any lock, sells any key.

uniate_priest.subject: The Uniate priest
uniate_priest.text: Father Hryhorij, the Uniate priest in Kazimierz, hears confessions no Latin priest will, and knows the sacristy of St Mary's from the old days.
line: Ojciec Hryhorij, unita z Kazimierza, spowiada tych, których nikt nie chce. Zna zakrystię Mariacką.
Father Hryhorij, the Uniate from Kazimierz, confesses those no one else will. He knows St Mary's sacristy.

sergeant_kleparz.subject: Sergeant Kmita
sergeant_kleparz.source: the veterans on the church steps
sergeant_kleparz.text: Old Sergeant Kmita of Racławice sells horses at Kleparz market beyond the Barbican, and still keeps his scythe on the wall.
line: Stary Kmita spod Racławic handluje końmi na Kleparzu. Kosę trzyma na ścianie.
Old Kmita of Racławice trades horses at Kleparz. Keeps his scythe on the wall.

raid_kazimierz.subject: Powder in Kazimierz
raid_kazimierz.text: Jacobins keep powder in a cellar in Kazimierz.
line: Jakobini trzymają proch w piwnicy na Kazimierzu.
Jacobins keep powder in a cellar in Kazimierz.
raid_kazimierz.plant_note: The watch goes to Kazimierz: the Rynek loses a patrol for a night. Kazimierz pays for it.

effects.text: The watch turned out half a company to search the cellars of Kazimierz. One patrol fewer walks the Rynek tonight.

disproved.text: No powder in Kazimierz, only frightened families. The Commandant wants to know who started the tale.

commissioner_debts.subject: Commissioner von Hauer
commissioner_debts.text: Commissioner von Hauer owes the Prussian bankers more than his salary.
line: Komisarz von Hauer winien Prusakom więcej, niż zarabia.
Commissioner von Hauer owes the Prussians more than he earns.
commissioner_debts.plant_note: True only if you hold the banker's notes. The magnates love a debtor's fall.

effects.text: In the salons they count the Commissioner's debts on their fingers. He will be a nervous host.

disproved.text: The Commissioner produced his accounts at the Governor's table. The salon looks foolish.

corporal_skims.subject: Corporal Brandt
corporal_skims.text: Corporal Brandt sells the garrison's firewood to the Jews of Kazimierz and pockets the price.
line: Kapral Brandt sprzedaje drewno garnizonu i chowa pieniądze do kieszeni.
Corporal Brandt sells the garrison's firewood and pockets the money.
corporal_skims.plant_note: True if Marianna has talked to you. A disgraced corporal is a corporal sent away.

effects.text: Corporal Brandt has been called to the Commandant about the firewood. St Mary's post stands without him.

disproved.text: The Corporal's woodpile was counted and found whole. Someone lied about him, and he wants to know who.

informer_russian.subject: The man in grey
informer_russian.text: The grey informer sells what he hears to the Russians as well as the Austrians.
line: Ten szary sprzedaje Moskalom to samo, co Austriakom.
The man in grey sells the Muscovites the same as he sells the Austrians.
informer_russian.plant_note: A trap for an enforcer: if it takes hold, the Austrians arrest their own informer.

effects.text: The Polizei took the grey informer from his lantern in irons. No one will point at your face there again.

disproved.text: The informer cleared his name, and he has a good idea whose tale it was.

amnesty.subject: An amnesty
amnesty.text: The Emperor grants an amnesty to deserters who report at the Town Hall by Sunday.
line: Cesarz daje amnestię dezerterom, co się zgłoszą do Ratusza do niedzieli.
The Emperor grants amnesty to deserters who report to the Town Hall by Sunday.
amnesty.plant_note: Draws a person into the open: the deserter comes into the Rynek to see if it is true.

effects.text: Deserters are creeping into the Rynek to read the notice board. The man from the tannery among them.

disproved.text: There was no amnesty. Two deserters were taken at the Town Hall door; the street blames whoever started it.

levies_marching.subject: The levies
levies_marching.text: The peasant levies of Kościuszko's villages are marching on the Florian Gate.
line: Chłopi z kosami idą na Bramę Floriańską. Jak w dziewięćdziesiątym czwartym.
Peasants with scythes are marching on the Florian Gate. Like in ninety-four.
levies_marching.plant_note: True if Sergeant Kmita is with you. Frightens the garrison, heartens the street.

effects.text: The garrison doubled the Florian Gate and the street is whispering 'Racławice'.

disproved.text: No scythes came. The garrison relaxes, and laughs.

bishop_sermon.subject: The Bishop's sermon
bishop_sermon.text: The Bishop will preach the Third of May from the pulpit of St Mary's on Sunday.
line: Biskup w niedzielę będzie kazał o Trzecim Maja. Z ambony Mariackiej!
On Sunday the Bishop will preach the Third of May. From St Mary's pulpit!
bishop_sermon.plant_note: True only if the Bishop has been turned. Crowds follow a bishop.

effects.text: The faithful talk of nothing but Sunday's sermon.

disproved.text: The Bishop denied it from the pulpit, coldly. The canons are furious with the movement.

russian_gold.subject: Russian gold
russian_gold.text: Russian gold pays the Austrian officers' gambling debts.
line: Moskiewskie złoto płaci karciane długi austriackich oficerów.
Muscovite gold pays the Austrian officers' card debts.
russian_gold.plant_note: True if you have met the Russian. Austrians trust each other less; Russia notices.

effects.text: Austrian officers eye each other over the card tables. The watch is sloppier for it.

disproved.text: The Russian envoy protested loudly. The Austrians look for the source.

rota_midnight.subject: The watch change
rota_midnight.text: At midnight the Cloth Hall sentry walks to St Mary's for the change: the passage stands empty for a few minutes.
line: O północy żołnierz spod Sukiennic idzie na zmianę. Przejście puste.
At midnight the Cloth Hall soldier goes to the change. The passage is empty.

salis_upstairs.subject: Captain von Salis
salis_upstairs.text: Captain von Salis of the garrison visits Mother Weronika's on Thursdays and owes her for a month.
line: Kapitan von Salis bywa u Matki Weroniki w czwartki. Winien jej za miesiąc.
Captain von Salis visits Mother Weronika on Thursdays. Owes her a month.

effects.text: Captain von Salis's Thursdays are known in every tavern. He will look away when asked nicely.

informer_master.subject: The informer's master
informer_master.text: The grey informer reports to the Corporal at St Mary's post, never to the Commandant: the Corporal keeps the reward.
line: Szary donosi kapralowi, nie komendantowi. Kapral bierze nagrodę.
The grey one reports to the Corporal, not the Commandant. The Corporal takes the reward.

ballad_third_may.subject: The ballad of the Third of May
ballad_third_may.text: A new ballad of the Third of May is sung under the Cloth Hall arcades, to a tune the Austrians think is a hymn.
line: Nowa piosenka o Trzecim Maja, na nutę kolędy. Austriacy myślą, że to pobożne.
A new song of the Third of May, to a carol tune. The Austrians think it's pious.

effects.text: The ballad of the Third of May is hummed in every queue for bread.

flogging_shame.subject: The flogging
flogging_shame.text: They flogged a boy for a seditious song under the Town Hall, and the crowd did not jeer: it wept.
line: Wychłostali chłopaka za piosenkę. Ludzie nie szydzili, płakali.
They flogged a boy for a song. People didn't jeer, they wept.

effects.text: The flogged boy's name is chalked on the Cloth Hall pillars.

bishop_names.subject: The Bishop's list
bishop_names.text: The Bishop's letter to Vienna named three 'Jacobin' priests for the Emperor's prisons.
line: Biskup posłał do Wiednia trzy nazwiska księży. Jakobinów, pisze.
The Bishop sent three priests' names to Vienna. Jacobins, he writes.

effects.text: Parish priests whisper the three names the Bishop sent to Vienna.

hauer_arnim.subject: The Commissioner's lieutenant
hauer_arnim.text: Commissioner von Hauer never goes anywhere without young Lieutenant von Arnim, and never lets him dance with the ladies.
line: Komisarz nigdzie bez porucznika von Arnima. I nie da mu tańczyć z pannami.
The Commissioner goes nowhere without Lieutenant von Arnim. Won't let him dance with the girls.

levies_ready.subject: The villages
levies_ready.text: The villages round Kraków have scythes straightened into pikes and wait for a signal from the city.
line: We wsiach kosy już na sztorc. Czekają na znak z miasta.
In the villages the scythes are already set upright. They wait for a sign from the city.

effects.text: Carters swear the villages have their scythes set upright and wait for the city's sign.

kollataj_letter.subject: Kołłątaj's letter
kollataj_letter.text: A letter from Hugo Kołłątaj, the Austrians' prisoner at Olomouc, is copied from hand to hand: 'the Constitution is not dead while one man reads it'. (The letter is fiction; his imprisonment is not.)
line: List od Kołłątaja z Ołomuńca krąży po mieście. Przepisują go po nocach.
A letter from Kołłątaj in Olomouc goes round the city. They copy it by night.

effects.text: Kołłątaj's letter from his Austrian prison is read aloud in the salons.

kosciuszko_escaped.subject: Kościuszko
kosciuszko_escaped.text: Kościuszko has escaped from St Petersburg and is riding for Kraków. (False: he is a prisoner of the Russians until 1796.)
line: Kościuszko uciekł z Petersburga! Jedzie na Kraków!
Kościuszko has escaped from Petersburg! He's riding for Kraków!

effects.text: The street talks of nothing but Kościuszko's escape. The garrison doubles the gates.

disproved.text: Kościuszko is still in the Tsar's prison. The disappointment is bitter.

boguslawski_tour.subject: The Krakowiacy
boguslawski_tour.text: Bogusławski's players are coming from Lwów to play the Krakowiacy i Górale in the Town Hall. (Only a rumour: his company stayed in Lwów.)
line: Bogusławski przyjedzie ze Lwowa grać Krakowiaków i Górali!
Bogusławski is coming from Lwów to play the Krakowiacy i Górale!

effects.text: The whole town hums the Krakowiacy airs, waiting for players who will not come.

weeping_icon.subject: The weeping icon
weeping_icon.text: The Madonna in St Mary's north aisle weeps real tears for Poland.
line: Matka Boska w Mariackim płacze! Prawdziwymi łzami, za Polskę!
Our Lady in St Mary's is weeping! Real tears, for Poland!
weeping_icon.plant_note: A miracle draws crowds to St Mary's (cover to blend in) and pulls the watch. If it is exposed as staged, the Church cries blasphemy.

effects.text: Crowds kneel on St Mary's steps day and night; the watch cannot move them.

disproved.text: The canons declared the tears to be damp. The crowds go home, disappointed and cold.

commissioner_curse.subject: The curse on the Commissioner
commissioner_curse.text: A Kazimierz wise-woman has cursed Commissioner von Hauer's house: his servants hear knocking in the walls.
line: Znachorka przeklęła dom komisarza. Służba słyszy stukanie w ścianach.
A wise-woman has cursed the Commissioner's house. The servants hear knocking in the walls.
commissioner_curse.plant_note: Servants desert, the guards grow uneasy (the watch sees a little less far at night).

effects.text: Two of the Commissioner's maids have run home to their villages, and the sentries cross themselves at the Town Hall.

marian_prophecy.subject: The Marian prophecy
marian_prophecy.text: A shepherdess at Kalwaria saw the Virgin, who promised the Commonwealth would rise again before the thaw.
line: Pastuszka w Kalwarii widziała Matkę Boską. Rzeczpospolita wstanie przed roztopami!
A shepherd girl at Kalwaria saw Our Lady. The Commonwealth will rise before the thaw!
marian_prophecy.plant_note: The street takes heart; the Bishop demands a say in what the Virgin promises. If it fails, it hurts everyone.

effects.text: Pilgrims set out for Kalwaria in the snow. The Bishop wants to know who is putting words in Our Lady's mouth.

disproved.text: The shepherdess recanted before the canons. A failed prophecy leaves everyone colder.

stanislaus_relic.subject: St Stanislaus' bone
stanislaus_relic.text: A bone of St Stanislaus, taken from Wawel before the Austrians came, will be carried before the rising.
line: Kość świętego Stanisława, wyniesiona z Wawelu, pójdzie przed powstaniem.
A bone of St Stanislaus, carried out of Wawel, will go before the rising.
stanislaus_relic.plant_note: A rallying object: the crowd follows a relic more easily (the riot needs less street loyalty).

effects.text: Old women kiss the air where the relic is said to have passed.

disproved.text: The Wawel chapter counted its relics: all present. The tale dies, and the canons are cross.

kosciuszko_sabre.subject: Kościuszko's sabre
kosciuszko_sabre.text: Kościuszko's sabre from Racławice is hidden in the city, waiting for a hand to lift it.
line: Szabla Kościuszki spod Racławic jest w mieście. Czeka na rękę.
Kościuszko's sabre from Racławice is in the city. It's waiting for a hand.
kosciuszko_sabre.plant_note: True if Kmita's veterans stand with you (the sergeant has a sabre, at least). The street rallies to it.

effects.text: Veterans touch their caps when they pass the Cloth Hall, as if a sabre hung there.

disproved.text: The sabre was an old cavalry blade from a pawnshop.

black_dog.subject: The black dog of Kazimierz
black_dog.text: A black dog with burning eyes runs the streets of Kazimierz at night: an omen, they say, sent by the Jews. (A dangerous tale: counter it before it takes hold.)
line: Czarny pies z ognistymi oczami biega nocą po Kazimierzu. Mówią, że to Żydzi go puszczają.
A black dog with fiery eyes runs through Kazimierz by night. They say the Jews let it loose.

counter.label: Counter the black-dog tale with the rabbi and the Uniate priest
counter.desc: Walk Kazimierz with Rabbi and Father Hryhorij, and say what the dog is: a tanner's mastiff. Salon +3, guilds loyalty +3, church loyalty -2.

effects.text: You walked Kazimierz with the rabbi and a Uniate priest, and named the black dog: a tanner's mastiff. The tale shrivels.
Stones were thrown at Kazimierz windows over a black dog. The guilds of Kazimierz will not forget who stood by.

disproved.text: The black dog turned out to be a tanner's mastiff with a cold. The tale dies.

hejnal_sign.subject: The broken hejnał
hejnal_sign.text: Last night the trumpeter on St Mary's tower broke off the hejnał mid-note, as for the Tatar arrow of old, and did not finish it: a sign.
line: Hejnał urwał się w pół nuty, jak za Tatarów. I nie skończył. To znak.
The hejnał broke off mid-note, like in the Tatar days. And didn't finish. It's a sign.

effects.text: People stop in the square at every hour to hear whether the hejnał breaks off again.

wilk_tithe.subject: Wilk
wilk_tithe.text: Wilk, the river king, takes a tenth of every barrel landed on the Vistula quays, and sells the smugglers who will not pay to the Austrians.
line: Wilk bierze dziesiątą beczkę z każdej barki. Kto nie płaci, tego sprzedaje Austriakom.
Wilk takes every tenth barrel off every barge. Anyone who won't pay, he sells to the Austrians.

wilk_cards.subject: Wilk's card game
wilk_cards.text: Wilk plays cards in the yard behind the fishermen's tavern on the quay from a quarter to ten, and drinks from his own jug.
line: Wilk gra w karty za karczmą rybacką od trzy kwadranse na dziesiątą. Pije z własnego dzbana.
Wilk plays cards behind the fishermen's tavern from a quarter to ten. Drinks from his own jug.

wilk_bathhouse.subject: Wilk's bath
wilk_bathhouse.text: Wilk takes the steam at the riverside bathhouse at twenty to eleven, with a jug of kvass and one bodyguard at the door.
line: Wilk chodzi do łaźni nad rzeką za dwadzieścia jedenasta. Kwas i jeden goryl przy drzwiach.
Wilk goes to the riverside bathhouse at twenty to eleven. Kvass, and one heavy at the door.

wilk_barge.subject: Wilk's barges
wilk_barge.text: Wilk inspects his salt barges himself at half past eleven, standing under the cargo hook.
line: Wilk sam ogląda barki o wpół do dwunastej. Stoi pod hakiem.
Wilk checks his barges himself at half past eleven. Stands right under the hook.

wilk_madam.subject: Wilk's take
wilk_madam.text: Mother Weronika pays Wilk a third of the red lantern's take, and Jędrek collects it and hates him for it.
line: Matka Weronika płaci Wilkowi trzecią część. Jędrek zbiera i nienawidzi go za to.
Mother Weronika pays Wilk a third. Jędrek collects it, and hates him for it.

raid_warehouse.subject: A raid on Wilk's warehouse
raid_warehouse.text: The Austrians will raid Wilk's warehouse on the quay tonight.
line: Austriacy dziś w nocy robią nalot na magazyn Wilka.
The Austrians are raiding Wilk's warehouse tonight.
raid_warehouse.plant_note: Pulls a bodyguard away from Wilk to guard the warehouse (it isolates him).

effects.text: Wilk has put one of his bodyguards and half his men on the warehouse doors, waiting for a raid.

disproved.text: No raid came. Wilk's men laugh, and look harder at strangers.

undercroft_grates.subject: The drains
undercroft_grates.text: The boys go in by the well grate: under the Rynek the old cellars are joined by brick drains all the way to the river outfall.
line: Chłopaki wchodzą przez kratę przy studni. Pod Rynkiem piwnice łączą się kanałami aż do Wisły.
The lads go in through the grate by the well. Under the square the cellars are joined by drains all the way to the Vistula.

fence_undercroft.subject: The fence below
fence_undercroft.text: Pan Kuna, the fence under the Rynek, buys anything in a cellar you reach by the well grate, and keeps a ledger of every thief in town.
line: Pan Kuna pod Rynkiem kupi wszystko. Wejście przez kratę przy studni. Ma księgę każdego złodzieja.
Pan Kuna under the square buys anything. In through the well grate. He keeps a book on every thief.

visits_rajca.subject: Who visits the red lantern
visits_rajca.text: Rajca Grodzicki visits the house with the red lantern on the second and fifth nights of the campaign.
line: Rajca Grodzicki chodzi pod czerwoną latarnię. We wtorki i w piątki.
Councillor Grodzicki goes under the red lantern. Tuesdays and Fridays.

visits_magistrate.subject: Who visits the red lantern
visits_magistrate.text: Magistrate Pölzl visits the house with the red lantern on the third and sixth nights of the campaign.
line: Sędzia Pölzl wchodzi tylnymi drzwiami do Matki Weroniki.
Judge Pölzl goes in by Mother Weronika's back door.

visits_clerk.subject: Who visits the red lantern
visits_clerk.text: The commissary's clerk visits the house with the red lantern on the second, fourth and seventh nights of the campaign.
line: Pisarz komisarza, Wlach, bywa na górze u Weroniki. Często.
The commissary's clerk, Wlach, is upstairs at Weronika's. Often.

visits_elder.subject: Who visits the red lantern
visits_elder.text: Master Lis of the goldsmiths visits the house with the red lantern on the fourth night of the campaign.
line: Stary Lis od złotników też chodzi pod latarnię, choć ma żonę jak dragon.
Old Lis of the goldsmiths goes under the lantern too, though his wife is a dragoon.

visits_canon.subject: Who visits the red lantern
visits_canon.text: A canon of the chapter visits the house with the red lantern on the fifth night of the campaign.
line: Kanonik Wąsowicz chodzi do Weroniki. Na spowiedź, mówi.
Canon Wąsowicz goes to Weronika's. To hear confession, he says.

visits_prussian.subject: Who visits the red lantern
visits_prussian.text: The Prussian agent Stolle visits the house with the red lantern on the third night of the campaign.
line: Prusak Stolle płaci u Weroniki talarami.
The Prussian Stolle pays at Weronika's in thalers.

visits_rusofficer.subject: Who visits the red lantern
visits_rusofficer.text: A Russian captain visits the house with the red lantern on the sixth night of the campaign.
line: Moskiewski rotmistrz Sablin ma pokój u Weroniki na szósty dzień.
The Muscovite captain Sablin has a room at Weronika's for the sixth day.

visits_steward.subject: Who visits the red lantern
visits_steward.text: A magnate's steward visits the house with the red lantern on the seventh night of the campaign.
line: Rządca Mrozowski przepija pańskie pieniądze u Weroniki.
The steward Mrozowski drinks his lord's money at Weronika's.

debts_rajca.subject: The councillor's debts
debts_rajca.text: Rajca Grodzicki owes Wilk three hundred złoty and dares not tell his wife.
line: Rajca Grodzicki winien Wilkowi trzysta złotych. Żona nie wie.
Councillor Grodzicki owes Wilk three hundred złoty. His wife doesn't know.

son_rajca.subject: The councillor's son
son_rajca.text: Rajca Grodzicki's son Marcin is at the Collegium and in with the Jacobin students; the Austrians have his name.
line: Syn rajcy, Marcin, siedzi z jakobinami na Kolegium. Austriacy mają jego nazwisko.
The councillor's son Marcin sits with the Jacobins at the Collegium. The Austrians have his name.

clerk_notes.subject: The clerk's notes
clerk_notes.text: The commissary's clerk Wlach has lost a year's salary at cards, and Herr Lindner holds his notes.
line: Pisarz Wlach przegrał roczną pensję w karty. Weksle ma Lindner.
The clerk Wlach lost a year's pay at cards. Lindner holds the notes.

steward_daughter.subject: The steward's daughter
steward_daughter.text: The steward Mrozowski's daughter Zosia wants to sing, and her father would do anything to keep her off the stage and out of the barracks' eye.
line: Córka rządcy, Zosia, chce śpiewać. Ojciec zrobi wszystko, żeby nie poszła na scenę.
The steward's daughter Zosia wants to sing. Her father would do anything to keep her off the stage.

blasphemy.text: The staged miracle was exposed: wax tears and a hidden pulley. The Church cries blasphemy, and it cries your name.
